overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Chair did not reasonably anticipate the unlisted Police Chief discussion raised by another selectman during Selectmen's Statements. The public-comment point appeared only in a footnote.

allegations.summary: Board discussed a Police Chief topic at its July 8, 2013 meeting that was not on the posted notice, though the Chair had declined a request to add it.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by discussing a topic unanticipated by the Chair.

allegations.summary: Complainant said the unlisted topic kept him from attending and addressing the Board during public statements; the AG only noted the Chair controls public address.
allegations.key_passage: We note that while a member of the public has the right to attend an open session of a meeting of a public body, that individual does not have the right to address the pubic body without the permission of the Chair.
